words.text: to get a call from an unknown number
not to be able to find the end of the sticky tape
to speak to a service engineer
words.translation: поговорить с сервисным инженером (мастером по обслуживанию)

words.text: Wouldn’t take no for an answer.
words.translation: Не принимаю отказ. / «Нет» и слышать не хочу.

words.text: This is ridiculous! I’ve been on hold for 10 minutes. I’ve got better things to do!
words.translation: Это смешно (издевательство)! Я вишу на линии уже 10 минут. У меня есть дела поважнее!

words.text: It’s a part of our drive to cut down on the use of plastic.
words.translation: Это часть инициативы (нашей кампании) по сокращению использования пластика.
телефонный продавец/агент (cold calling – contacting potential customers by phone without having spoken to them or received their permission beforehand, usually to sell something)

words.text: to face sth / to be faced with sth
words.example: She had to face the consequences of her decision. We were faced with a difficult choice when the company announced job cuts.

words.text: to put forward (a more positive view)
to tell the truth / to tell a lie
to ask for time off from your work

words.translation: под самый конец рабочего дня в пятницу

words.text: Everyone has their mind on other things at those times.
words.translation: В такое время у всех мысли совсем о другом.

words.text: to take the time (to make a list of your achievements)
words.translation: уделить время (тому, чтобы составить список своих достижений)

words.text: to mix your personal life and your professional life

words.translation: Точно так же, … / В равной степени, …

words.text: On that topic, (if your boss says no, it’s important…)
words.translation: Кстати об этом / Возвращаясь к этой теме (если начальник откажет, важно…)

words.text: to be committed to the company

words.example: I'd like to work abroad in the future. Please make sure you arrive on time in future.

words.text: to give one other piece of advice
(He was made redundant soon after his request), which just goes to show!
words.translation: (Его сократили вскоре после его просьбы), что лишний раз это подтверждает!

words.text: to access all the information in a handy document
words.translation: получить доступ ко всей информации в удобном файле (документе)

words.text: to go on a business trip
to find the only other person (in a lift)
words.translation: оказаться наедине с другим человеком (в лифте)

words.text: Office politics is a fraught [frɔːt] game.
words.translation: Офисные интриги (политика) – игра опасная (полная подводных камней). fraught – удручающий (=worrying or difficult)
подать официальную жалобу (=to make an official complaint about a problem; to lodge – подавать заявление)
words.example: I eventually lodged a formal complaint after several unsuccessful attempts to contact customer service.

words.text: to be entitled to a refund ['riːfʌnd]
words.example: If the product is faulty, you may be entitled to a full refund.

words.translation: оправдать потраченные деньги (=to receive good value for the money you have spent)
words.example: The service was so poor that I certainly didn't get my money's worth.

words.text: to take something up with someone
words.translation: обратиться к кому-либо по какому-либо вопросу; поднять вопрос перед кем-либо (=to discuss a problem with someone who can help resolve it)
words.example: If the issue isn't resolved, I'll take it up with the manager.

words.translation: прощупать почву (=to try something or find out people's reactions before making a decision)
words.example: I decided to test the waters by asking my boss how he felt about flexible working hours before formally requesting a change.

words.text: to have second thoughts about sth
words.translation: усомниться в чём-либо (=to start having doubts about a decision)
words.example: I had second thoughts about buying the extended warranty after reading the small print.

words.text: to bring sth to someone's attention
words.example: I'd like to bring a problem with my latest bill to your attention.

words.text: to be under no obligation to do sth
words.example: You're under no obligation to accept their offer straight away.

words.text: to take a toll on sb
words.translation: негативно сказываться на ком-либо (=to have a serious negative effect on someone's health, energy or well-being)
words.example: Constant interruptions and unrealistic deadlines can take a toll on your mental health.

words.text: to come to terms with sth
words.translation: смириться с чем-либо (=to gradually accept a difficult or unpleasant situation)
words.example: It took me a while to come to terms with the fact that I wasn't getting a pay rise.

words.text: to go to the trouble of doing sth
words.translation: потрудиться сделать что-либо; приложить усилия (=to make a special effort to do something, often when it is inconvenient)
words.example: She went to the trouble of preparing a detailed report, but nobody bothered to read it.
Employees' personal circumstances are sometimes given little consideration when redundancies are announced.

words.text: to get caught up in sth
words.translation: увлечься чем-либо; оказаться втянутым во что-либо (=to become involved in something, often without intending to)
words.example: It's easy to get caught up in office politics and lose sight of what really matters.
